rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After maximal effort still fails to produce anything comparable, the challenge establishes the Qur’an’s miraculousness and makes belief and Godfearing obligatory.
rows.anchor: إذا بذلتم في السعي غاية المجهود وجاوزتم في الحد كل حد معهود متشبثين بالذيول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional particle despite their certain inability taunts them and exposes their foolish reliance on eloquence; it may be ironic metaphor, literal, or a convention contrary to the apparent situation.
rows.anchor: وأتى بأن والمقام اذا العجز وهو سبحانه وتعالى اللطيف الخبير تهكما بهم كما يقول الواثق بالغلبة لخصمه

rows.speaker: ابن هشام
rows.claim: Ibn Hisham denies syntactic competition between particles because they do not denote events and therefore do not seek complements.
rows.anchor: وقد صرح إبن هشام بأنه لا يكون بين الحروف لأنها لا دلالة لها على الحدث

rows.speaker: إبن العلج
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿAlj allows competition between إن and لم on the basis of this verse, but the author reports the objection that they differ in polarity, violating the condition of semantic sameness.
rows.anchor: إلا أن إبن العلج أجازه إستدلالا بهذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author explains their coexistence by taking إن to govern the whole clause, as though it said, “if you abandon the act”; this yields continued failure beginning in the past.
rows.anchor: فإن هنا داخلة على المجموع عاملة في محله كأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He leaves an unresolved parsing problem: it is unclear whether the syntactic locus belongs to the verb, the clause, or both, and extracting a verb from what follows seems unsatisfactory.
rows.anchor: قيل في ذلك إشكال لم يحرر دفعه بعد بما يشفي العليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generic “act” concisely makes attempting the commanded feat the test, since producing the object is impossible; the conditional consequence follows their inability to perform it.
rows.anchor: عبر سبحانه عن الفعل الخاص حيث كان الظاهر فإن لم تأتوا بسورة من مثله بالفعل المطلق العام ظاهرا لإيجاز القصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes “act” as naming the necessary act while intending its associated object, or as avoiding repetition by replacing an explicit noun with a pronoun.
rows.anchor: أطلق الفعل وأريد به الإتيان مع ما يتعلق به على طريقة ذكر اللازم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لن denies a future event, specializes in the imperfect, and governs the subjunctive, though a poetic exception is cited; it does not by itself make the denial eternal.
rows.anchor: ( لن ) يخب الآن من رجاك ومن حرك من دون بابك الحلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although لن adds emphasis and force, the author rejects claims that it entails perpetual negation or a long or short duration.
rows.anchor: ولا تقتضي النفي على التأييد وإن أفادت التأكيد والتشديد ولا طول مدة أو قلتها خلافا لبعضهم

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: A derivation reported from al-Khalil makes لن originate in أن: the hamza was dropped through frequent use, then the alif at the meeting of two quiescent letters.
rows.anchor: روى عن الخليل : فحذفت الهمزة لكثرتها وسقطت الألف للساكنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic line containing لا أن is offered for the derivation, but the possibility that أن is extra weakens its evidentiary force.
rows.anchor: يرجى المرء ما ( لا أن ) يلاقيه ويعرض دون أقربه الخطوب

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ derives لن from لا with its alif changed to nūn; the author rejects this as unmotivated and contrary to the ordinary principle.
rows.anchor: ولا لاكما عند الفراء فأبدلت ألفه نونا إذ لا داعي إلى ذلك وهو خلاف الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of future inability is parenthetical between the two parts of the conditional, reinforcing its premise and the obligation in its consequence.
rows.anchor: والجملة إعتراض بين جزئي الشرطية ظاهرا مقرر لمضمون مقدمها ومؤكد لإيجاب العمل بتاليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The categorical prediction is a manifest miracle of foreknowledge: a comparable challenge would have been widely transmitted given the motive to report it; Musaylima’s words were not meant as a contest.
rows.anchor: وهذه معجزة باهرة حيث أخبر بالغيب الخاص علمه به سبحانه وقد وقع الأمر كذلك كيف لا ولو عارضوه بشيء يدانيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative is the conditional answer; avoiding the Fire can stand for recognizing the miracle and believing in it, or for faith itself, so its conditional attachment is meaningful.
rows.anchor: جواب للشرط على أن إلتقاء النار كناية عن ظهور إعجازه المقتضي للتصديق والإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This interpretation answers the objection that avoidance of Hell is always required and that inability to produce a match is neither its cause nor necessary condition; some instead posit an implicit answer.
rows.anchor: يندفع ما يتوهم من أن إتقاء النار لازم من غير توقف على هذا الشرط فما معنى التعليق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa, وقود ordinarily means fuel, the thing by which a fire is lit; the form فعول commonly names an instrument or thing acted upon, though it can be a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: والوقود بالفتح كما قرأ به الجمهور ما يوقد به النار وكذا كل ما كان على فعول أسم لما يفعل به في المشهور

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr reads وقيدها, a variant the author records without further argument.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبيد بن عمير وقيدها

rows.speaker: عيسى بن عمرو
rows.claim: ʿĪsā ibn ʿAmr and others read the word with ḍamma; if it is a noun for fuel, its sense matches the common reading.
rows.anchor: وعيسى بن عمرو وغيره ( وقودها ) بالضم فإن كان اسما لما يوقد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the ḍamma reading is a verbal noun, its predication of the Fire is explained by emphasis, figurative transfer or comparison, or an implied possessive or burning.
rows.anchor: وإن كان مصدراكما قيل في سائر ما كان على فعول فحمله على النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi reports Ibn Mālik’s analysis: حجارة is the plural of حجر, with أحجار as the paucity plural; Ibn Mālik calls حجارة a collective noun because its pattern commonly occurs among singular nouns, which Alusi finds apparent.
rows.anchor: إنه اسم جمع لغلبة وزنه في المفردات وهو الظاهر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Reports from Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd identify the stones as sulfur; the author says this is the sounder view among hadith scholars.
rows.anchor: والمراد بها على ما صح عن إبن عباس وإبن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنهم ولمثل ذلك حكم الرفع حجارة الكبريت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sulfur intensifies the Fire through extreme heat, rapid ignition, adhesion to bodies, and the inmates’ becoming fuel; its stench, smoke, and density heighten the warning, though the next world exceeds worldly comparison.
rows.anchor: وفيها من شدة الحر وكثرة الإلتهاب وسرعة الإيقاد ومزيد الإلتصاق بالأبدان وإعداد أهل النار أن يكونوا حطبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation identifies the stones as carved idols, joined with their worshippers to increase their remorse when events contradict their expectations.
rows.anchor: المراد بها الأصنام التي ينحتونها وقرنها بهم في الآخرة زيادة لتحسرهم حيث بدا لهم نقيض ما كانوا يتوقعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idol interpretation is supported by the verse saying that worshippers and what they worship apart from God are Hell’s fuel; Ibn ʿArabī’s words also hint at it.
rows.anchor: ويؤيد هذا قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lexicon-based proposal takes the stones to mean gold and silver, which are also called حجر; the author regards it as weaker than the sulfur and idol readings.
rows.anchor: وحملها على الذهب والفضة لأنهما يسميان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among the two stronger identifications, hadith scholars prefer sulfur, whereas Zamakhsharī prefers the idol interpretation and Ibn ʿArabī hints at it.
rows.anchor: الأصح أولهما عند المحدثين وثانيهما عند الزمخشري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article on Fire is not, in the author’s view, generic; some scholars take it universally, meaning the Fire is fully capable of consuming both kinds of fuel.
rows.anchor: وأل فيها على كل ليست للعموم وذهب بعض أهل العلم إلى أنها له ويكون المعنى أن النار التي وعدوا بها صالحة لأن تحرق ما ألقى فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming people and stones magnifies Hell’s severity and makes the warning more frightening; a nonliteral reading conflicts with the apparent verses and risks impugning divine power.
rows.anchor: تعظيما لشأن جهنم وتنبيها على شدة وقودها ليقع ذلك من النفوس أعظم موقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning only people and stones does not exclude jinn and devils from Hell, since other passages establish their presence there.
rows.anchor: ولا يتوهم من الإقتصار على هذين الجنسين أن لا يكون في النار غيرهما

rows.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿArabī says people are Hell’s flames and idols its embers.
rows.anchor: قال سيدي الشيخ الأكبر قدس سره : أنهم لهبها وأولئك جمرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People precede stones because they perceive pain, or because their flesh, fat, and skin make them more combustible, intensifying the warning.
rows.anchor: وبدأ سبحانه بالناس لأنهم الذين يدركون الآلام أو لكونهم أكثر إيقادا من الجماد لما فيهم من الجلود واللحوم والشحوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fire is definite as an already known story because the description had appeared in Sūrat al-Taḥrīm; the author notes that the claim that al-Taḥrīm came first is disputed.
rows.anchor: لأن المنكر في سورة التحريم نزل أولا فسمعوه بصفته فلما نزل هذا بعد جاء معهودا فعرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preparation clause is detached from the preceding relative description to give the warning independent emphasis, as an independent statement of the Fire’s preparation.
rows.anchor: إبتداء كلام قطع عما قبله مع أن مقتضى الظاهر أن يعطف على الصلة السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the clause an answer to “why is its fuel so?” fails because the context does not prompt that question and the answer does not explain it.
rows.anchor: أما الثاني فلأن المقصد من الصلة التهويل فالسؤال بلم كان شأن النار كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parsing أعدت as a circumstantial clause from Fire, with an implied قد, is weak: its restriction is unnatural, and taking its predicate from the preceding clause creates an awkward separation.
rows.anchor: وجعله حالا من النار بإضمار قد والخبر من أجزاء الصلة لذي الحال

rows.speaker: الإمام المرزوقي
rows.claim: Al-Marzūqī allows أعدت as a second relative clause; multiple clauses of description or predication may occur with or without a conjunction.
rows.anchor: إنها صلة بعد صلة وتعدد الصلات كالصفات والأخبار كثير بعاطف وبدونه كما نص عليه الإمام المرزوقي

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Mālik allows coordination with the conjunction omitted; treating وقودها الناس as parenthetical or circumstantial is an unsuitable parsing.
rows.anchor: أو معطوف بحذف الحرف كما صرح به إبن مالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أعدت means “made ready.”
rows.anchor: ومعنى ( أعدت ) هيئت وقرأ عبد الله

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads أعتدت, from العتاد, meaning preparation or provision.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله أعتدت من العتاد بمعنى العدة

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads أعدها الله, explicitly naming God as the one who prepared it.
rows.anchor: وإبن أبي عبلة أعدها الله للكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may mean disbelievers as a class, with the addressees included foremost, or these addressees alone; an explicit noun can replace their pronoun to censure and explain the judgment.
rows.anchor: والمراد إما جنسهم والمخاطبون داخلون فيهم دخولا أوليا أو هم خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preparation for disbelievers does not bar others from entering incidentally, so there is no need to posit a different Fire for sinful believers.
rows.anchor: وكون الأعداد للكافرين لا ينافي دخول غيرهم فيها على جهة التطفل فلا حاجة إلى القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent verse indicates that Hell is already created; treating the future as a completed past because it is certain, as the Muʿtazilites do, is against the apparent sense.
rows.anchor: يتبادر من الآية الكريمة أن النار مخلوقة الآن

rows.speaker: أهل الكشف
rows.claim: People of spiritual unveiling hold that Hell is created but unfinished: it is presently burning air without embers, its keepers praise God, and human and jinn deeds produce its pains and changing punishments.
rows.anchor: والذي ذهب أهل الكشف إليه أنها مخلوقة غير أنها لم تتم وهي الآن عندهم دار حرروها هواء محترق لا جمر لها البتة

rows.speaker: عبدالله بن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar, seeing the sea, asked when it would become fire, disliked ablution with its water, and preferred dry ablution, citing the oceans being kindled.
rows.anchor: عبدالله بن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author describes bodily fire affecting the body’s exterior senses and a spiritual fire reaching hearts and punishing the directing soul; arrogant ignorance of God is itself severe torment.
rows.anchor: وهي ناران حسية مسلطة على ظاهر الجسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exact state of the afterlife cannot be known by people immersed in worldly ties; accept what the truthful Prophet reported when it is not impossible and entrust its reality to God.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة الأمر عندي لا يعلمها إلا الله تعالى ولا شيء أحسن من التسليم لما جاء به النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address turns back to the earlier addressees after cataloguing their offenses; direct address rebukes more sharply than speaking of them in the third person, which might not reach them.
rows.anchor: التفات إلى خطاب أولئك بعد أن عدد قبائحهم المستدعية لمزيد سخطه تعالى عليهم والإنكار إذا وجه إلى المخاطب كان أبلغ

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh treats كيف as an adverb and therefore always accusative.
rows.anchor: اسم إما ظرف وعزى إلى سيبويه فمحلها نصب دائما

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash does not treat كيف as an adverb: it is nominative with a subject and accusative with other predicates.
rows.anchor: أو غير ظرف وعزى إلى الأخفش فمحلها رفع مع المبتدأ ونصب مع غيره

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Mālik says no one calls كيف an adverb because it denotes neither place nor time; Ibn Hishām approves calling it one metaphorically because it means “in what state.”
rows.anchor: وادعى ابن مالك أن أحدا لم يقل بظرفيتها إذ ليست زمانا ولا مكانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كيف is mostly interrogative and only rarely conditional; jussive use is unattested, though Kufans and Quṭrub allow it by analogy, and Ibn Mawhab’s claim that it can coordinate is dismissed.
rows.anchor: وأكثر ما تستعمل استفهاما والشرط بها قليل والجزم غير مسموع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here كيف combines a question with denial, astonishment, and rebuke, asking how they can disbelieve whether ignorant of God or aware of Him.
rows.anchor: وهي هنا للإستخبار منضما إليه الإنكار والتعجيب لكفرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they know the account of their origin and end, they know a perfect Creator; acting despite this powerful deterrent is astonishing, and the wording charges them with obstinate disbelief.
rows.anchor: وهو يستلزم العلم بصانع موصوف بصفات الكمال منزه عن النقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كيف intensifies the rebuke beyond a plain “you disbelieve”: denying any state that must accompany existence implies, by proof, denial of the disbeliever’s existence; it can also negate every conceivable state of disbelief.
rows.anchor: التي لا تنفك ويلزم من نفيها نفى صاحبها بطريق البرهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine questioning need not imply ignorance: a request for information may alert or rebuke the hearer; the interrogative can seek that understanding occur in someone who lacks it, without combining literal and figurative meanings.
rows.anchor: لأنه إما أن يكون بمعنى طلب الخبر فلا نسلم المحالية إذ قد يكون لتنبيه المخاطب وتوبيخه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author explains divine astonishment as directed toward the addressee or as expressing its intended effect; alternatively, it is handled according to the Salaf’s approach.
rows.anchor: وكذا لا استحالة في وقوع التعجيب منه تعالى بل قالوا إذا ورد التعجب من الله جل وعلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect tense condemns continuing disbelief, not merely past disbelief, so the wording does not reproach those who later believed, such as most Companions.
rows.anchor: وأتى سبحانه بتكفرون ولم يأت بالماضي وإن كان الكفر قد وقع منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause before ثم is a circumstantial clause attached to the subject of تكفرون, with قد necessarily understood; it means “how can you disbelieve when He created you?”
rows.anchor: بتقدير قد لا محالة خلافا لمن وهم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation is a state that should prevent disbelief because human nature and reason are disposed to recognize that God alone creates.
rows.anchor: ولما كان مركوزا في الطباع ومخلوقا في العقول أن لا خالق إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clauses after the first may be resumptive rather than part of the circumstantial clause, since their conjunctions and forms differ; a stronger alternative treats the whole account as the state known to the addressees.
rows.anchor: والجمل بعد مستأنفة لا تعلق لها بالحال ولذا غايرت ما قبلها بالحرف والصيغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life is defined as a power arising from species-level equilibrium that gives rise to other powers; another definition is sensory capacity, though paralysis shows absent sensation can result from an impediment rather than absent life.
rows.anchor: والحياة قوة تتبع الإعتدال النوعي ويفيض منها سائر القوى وقيل القوة الحساسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those defining life by sensation likely mean touch: different senses belong to different organs, some animals lack particular senses, and identifying life with each would multiply or compose life in one individual.
rows.anchor: وكأنهم أرادوا من ذلك قوة اللمس لأن مغايرة الحياة لما عداه من الحواس ظاهرة فإنها مختصة بعضو دون عضو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life is also used figuratively for growth and for human perfections such as intellect, knowledge, and faith; death is the opposite at each level, while divine life denotes God’s perfection in knowledge and power.
rows.anchor: وتطلق مجازا على القوة النامية لأنها من طلائعها ومقدماتها وعلى ما يخص الإنسان من الفضائل كالعقل والعلم والإيمان

words: وَكُنتُمْ أَمْوَٰتًۭا فَأَحْيَٰكُمْ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يُحْيِيكُمْ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd, and Mujāhid takes the first death as prior nonexistence, the first life as creation, the second death as ordinary death, and the final life as resurrection.
rows.anchor: والمروي عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود ومجاهد رضي الله تعالى عنهم أن المراد بالموت الأول العدم السابق والأحياء الأول الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exacting scholars choose the prior-nonexistence reading, supported by “you were dead” and the final death’s attribution to God.
rows.anchor: واختاره بعض المحققين وادعى أن قوله تعالى ﴿ وكنتم أمواتا ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes “dead” as the embryonic stages until ensoulment, the first life as breathing of the spirit after those stages, and the later death and resurrection in their ordinary senses.
rows.anchor: واختار آخرون أن كونهم أمواتا هو من وقت استقرارهم نطفا في الأرحام إلى تمام الأطوار بعدها

rows.speaker: الساليكوتي
rows.claim: Al-Sālikūtī’s explanation makes the embryonic bodies like the dead; whether this is figurative depends on defining death as loss of prior life, while absolute absence of life makes it literal, the common view.
rows.anchor: قاله الساليكوتي ويفهم كلام بعضهم أنه على معنى كالأموات على التفسير الثاني وإن فسر بعدم الحياة مطلقا كان حقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most remote reading makes the first death ordinary death and the first life the grave’s questioning, using past tense for a certain future event.
rows.anchor: وأبعد الأقوال عندي حمل الموت الأول على المعهود بعد انقضاء الأجل والأحياء الأول على ما يكون للمسألة في القبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse does not prove that grave punishment is absent: its silence about a life enabling such punishment is no evidence against it, and other proofs establish the matter.
rows.anchor: ثم لا دليل في الآية على المختار لنفي عذاب القبر إذ نهاية ما فيها عدم ذكر الأحياء المصحح له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return to God does not prove that God occupies a place; it means assembly at the Resurrection, where He alone judges and command belongs to Him.
rows.anchor: لأن المراد بالرجوع إليه الجمع في المحشر حيث لا يتولى الحكم سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive reading of ترجعون suits the verse-ending rhyme and the preceding sense; the author calls it more eloquent than the active reading of Yaʿqūb, Mujāhid, and others.
rows.anchor: على البناء للمفعول دون يرجعكم المناسب للسياق مراعاة للتناسب رءوس الآي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the disbelievers may doubt God’s role and not know future events, manifest rational and revealed signs make such knowledge available and remove their excuse.
rows.anchor: لأن تمكنهم من العلم لوضوح الأدلة آفاقية وأنفسية وسطوع أنوارها عقلية ونقلية منزل منزل العلم في إزاحة العذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The audience may include believers as well as unbelievers: after proofs of monotheism and prophethood, warning and promise, the passage counts common and Israelite blessings; death is a blessing as a passage to eternal life and reunion.
rows.anchor: أكد ذلك بأن عدد عليهم النعم العامة

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ reads the stages inwardly: dead in outwardness, brought to life through unveiling of secrets, then dying to servitude’s traits and living through divine qualities.
rows.anchor: ومن الإشارة قول ابن عطاء

rows.speaker: فارس
rows.claim: Fāris reads the stages as moving from the servants’ witnessing to God’s witnessing, then their own witnessing dies away until they return wholly to God.
rows.anchor: وقال فارس ﴿ وكنتم أمواتا ﴾ بشواهدكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation clause joins the preceding account without a conjunction, either as its result or to mark that it independently conveys its point; it announces another blessing dependent on the first because benefit requires life.
rows.anchor: معطوف على قوله تعالى ﴿ وكنتم ﴾ وترك الحرف إما لكونه كالنتيجة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made everything on earth for people’s benefit: directly or indirectly in worldly affairs, and in religious affairs through inference and reflection.
rows.anchor: خلق لأجلكم جميع ما في الأرض لتنتفعوا به في أمور دنياكم بالذات أو بالواسطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هو is a third-person pronoun with dialectal forms: its wāw may be lightened or omitted in poetry, doubled in Himyar, and quiescent in Asad and Qays.
rows.anchor: لغير المتكلم والمخاطب وفيه لغات تخفيف الواو مفتوحة وحذفها في الشعر وتشديدها

rows.speaker: أهل الله
rows.claim: The people of God treat هو as a divine name indicating the uniquely specified essence, free of every kind of multiplicity.
rows.anchor: عند أهل الله تعالى اسم من أسمائه تعالى ينبىء عن كنه حقيقته المخصوصة المبرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One mystical-linguistic account makes هو a two-letter compound whose hāʾ is original and wāw extra; because wāw drops in dual and plural, it ultimately signals the one, sole existent.
rows.anchor: اسم مركب من حرفين الهاء والواو والهاء أصل والواو زائدة بدليل سقوطها في التثنية والجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same account says spiritual elders made هو the center of remembrance and lamp of the inward secret, repeated with each breath, while its referent eludes perception and analogy.
rows.anchor: ولمزيد ما فيه من الأسرار اتخذه الأجلة مدارا لذكرهم وسراجا لسرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the pronoun the subject and the relative phrase its predicate itself signals God’s majesty; putting “for you” before the direct object hastens the glad tidings.
rows.anchor: الضمير مبتدأ والموصول خبرا من الدلالة على الجلالة ما لا يخفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many Sunnī Ḥanafī and Shāfiʿī jurists and most Muʿtazilites infer from the verse that beneficial things are permissible before revealed law; al-Rāzī and al-Bayḍāwī choose this position.
rows.anchor: واستدل كثير من أهل السنة الحنفية والشافعية بالآية على إباحة الأشياء النافعة قبل ورود الشرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against the benefit-based inference, some note that the lām can have other uses, as in “if you do evil, it is against you”; the reply treats its association as beneficial ownership or particularization.
rows.anchor: واعترض بأن اللام تجيء لغير النفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Restricting the benefit to religious inference is contrary to the apparent sense; since every accountable person can infer from creation, the wording should extend to other benefits too.
rows.anchor: وبأن المراد النفع بالإستدلال وأجيب بأن التخصيص خلاف الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other positions hold that things default to prohibition before a prohibition is stated, or suspend judgment because the evidence appears conflicting.
rows.anchor: وذهب قوم إلى أن الأصل في الأشياء قبل الحظر وقال قوم بالوقف لتعارض الأدلة عندهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Libertarians argue that because everything is created for all, no one may have exclusive possession; the verse instead allows collective benefit alongside warranted individual assignments, determined by separate evidence.
rows.anchor: واستدلت الإباحية بالآية على مدعاهم قائلين إنها تدل على أن ما في الأرض جميعا خلق للكل فلا يكون لأحد اختصاص بشيء أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما can include everything on earth, even the earth itself, if “earth” means the lower region; alternatively the encompassing Throne or a conceptual direction explains how it can be included.
rows.anchor: تعم جميع ما في الأرض لأنفسها إذ لا يكون الشيء ظرفا لنفسه إلا أن يراد بها جهة السفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation includes every part of the earth because parts are necessary to it and their distinction from the whole is conceptual; the author rejects adding “and the earth” as an explicit omitted object.
rows.anchor: نعم قيل تعم كل جزء من أجزاء الأرض فإنه من جملة ضروراتها ما فيها ضرورة وجود الجزء في الكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جميعا is an emphatic circumstantial accusative from ما, not evidence that all things were created simultaneously; taking it from لكم or الأرض conflicts with the context and emphasis.
rows.anchor: ولا دلالة لهما كما ذكره البعض على الإجتماع الزماني

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabīʿ explains استوى إلى السماء as rising and ascending toward it without specifying how, likening it, or delimiting it.
rows.anchor: أي علا إليها وارتفع من غير تكييف ولا تمثيل ولا تحديد قاله الربيع

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains it as turning toward the heaven with an unimpeded, straight intention, from the expression for aiming like a released arrow.
rows.anchor: أو قصد إليها بإرادته قصدا سويا بلا صارف يلويه ولا عاطف يثنيه من قولهم استوى إليه كالسهم المرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation takes استوى as prevailed over and possessed, supported by a line describing conquerors who rose over their foes.
rows.anchor: وقيل استولى وملك كما في قوله فلما علونا واستوينا عليهم تركناهم صرعى لنسر وكاسر
